items.question: Do I need a CMS to use Astro Launchpad?
items.answer: No. You can use plain Markdown files as your content source. A CMS (Directus, Sanity, etc.) is entirely optional and added via a feature pack.

items.question: Can I use Tailwind CSS?
items.answer: Yes. Tailwind is a feature pack you opt into during project generation. The base template uses semantic HTML and CSS variables.

items.question: Is this locked to any hosting provider?
items.answer: No. Astro Launchpad generates a standard Astro project. You can deploy anywhere Astro supports — Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare, Docker, and more.

items.question: What is AI-kit?
items.answer: AI-kit is an optional set of Markdown prompts, skill files, and JSON schemas that help you generate copy, review SEO, model CMS content, and document your project for AI coding agents.

blog_posts.title: Getting Started with Astro Launchpad
blog_posts.excerpt: Learn how to scaffold your first Astro Launchpad site in under five minutes using the CLI.
blog_posts.content:
# Getting Started with Astro Launchpad

Astro Launchpad is a CLI-first starter for building editable landing pages with Astro. In this guide, you'll scaffold a project, explore the block system, and connect it to Directus.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 22+
- pnpm 11+

## Create a new project

```bash
pnpm create astro-launchpad@latest my-site
```

Follow the interactive prompts to choose a preset and CMS.

## Project structure

After scaffolding, you'll have:

- `src/lib/content/` — content provider interface and implementations
- `src/lib/blocks/` — Zod schemas for block validation
- `src/components/blocks/` — Astro block components
- `src/content/` — your Markdown content files

## Next steps

Switch to Directus by updating the import in your page to use `directusProvider` instead of `markdownProvider`.

blog_posts.title: Connecting Directus to Your Astro Site
blog_posts.excerpt: A step-by-step guide to applying the Directus schema, seeding content, and wiring up the DirectusContentProvider.
blog_posts.content:
# Connecting Directus to Your Astro Site

The Directus feature pack ships with a schema snapshot, a seed script, and a typed `DirectusContentProvider`. Here's how to wire everything together.

## 1. Start Directus

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

Directus will be available at http://localhost:8055.

## 2. Apply the schema

```bash
npx directus schema apply ./schema/snapshot.json
```

## 3. Create a static API token

In the Directus admin (Settings → Access Tokens), create a token with read access to all content collections.

## 4. Set environment variables

```bash
# .env
DIRECTUS_URL=http://localhost:8055
DIRECTUS_TOKEN=your-token-here
```

## 5. Seed content

```bash
npx tsx seed/seed.ts
```

## 6. Use the provider

In your Astro page, swap the import:

```ts
import { directusProvider } from '../lib/content';
const page = await directusProvider.getPage('home');
```
